Plan melting operations according to production requirements, approved steel grades, raw material availability, and billet specifications. Monitor furnace operating conditions, melting progress, bath temperature, power consumption, melting cycle time, and molten steel readiness. Monitor melting productivity, furnace utilization, heat cycle time, metal recovery, and production losses. Identify operational problems affecting melting efficiency, steel quality, and production continuity, and implement corrective measures. Chemical Composition & Steel Grade Control Ensure that molten steel and finished billets meet the approved chemical composition requirements for the specified steel grade. Coordinate with the laboratory team for representative sampling and chemical analysis using available testing equipment, including spectrometers where installed. Monitor the control of carbon, manganese, silicon, sulfur, phosphorus, and other specified alloying or residual elements as applicable to the approved steel grade. Review test results and coordinate necessary corrective actions before molten steel is released for casting. Ensure proper control and documentation of alloy additions, deoxidizers, and other approved steelmaking materials. Maintain heat-wise chemical composition records, material traceability, and test documentation. Investigate chemical composition deviations, material mix-ups, and recurring quality issues to prevent non-conforming steel production. Molten Steel Temperature & Process Control Monitor molten steel temperature at critical stages of melting, tapping, ladle handling, and casting. Coordinate with furnace and casting operators to maintain appropriate temperature ranges according to the approved process and casting requirements. Prevent operational delays that may cause excessive temperature loss, unnecessary holding time, or unstable casting conditions. Ensure proper tapping practices, slag carryover control, and safe transfer of molten steel. Coordinate ladle preparation, refractry condition monitoring, and equipment readiness with the responsible teams. Analyze temperature-related casting defects and production losses and implement suitable process improvements. Continuous Casting & Billet Manufacturing Supervise continuous casting machine operations, where installed, including tundish preparation, casting sequence, mould operation, cooling water systems, withdrawal speed, and billet cutting. Ensure stable casting conditions and proper coordination between molten steel supply and casting capacity. Monitor billet dimensions, surface condition, straightness, identification, and heat-wise traceability. Coordinate with the Quality Control team to inspect billet quality and identify surface cracks, internal defects, segregation, porosity, and other casting-related abnormalities where applicable. Monitor casting interruptions, rejected billets, metal losses, and production yield. Ensure proper cooling, handling, storage, and segregation of billets according to quality and production requirements. Billet Quality & Metallurgical Defect Prevention Establish and implement billet inspection and acceptance procedures in coordination with Quality Control. Investigate billet defects such as surface cracks, corner cracks, inclusions, seams, segregation, internal porosity, and dimensional irregularities. Identify the relationship between raw material quality, chemical composition, melting practice, casting conditions, and downstream rolling defects. Ensure that rejected or suspect billets are identified, segregated, and prevented from entering production without the required approval. Coordinate root-cause analysis and corrective actions for recurring billet quality problems. Maintain billet heat numbers, batch identification, inspection records, and traceability throughout the production process. Steel Yield, Metallic Recovery & Consumption Control Monitor metallic charge consumption, molten steel output, casting yield, billet recovery, and process losses. Analyze melting loss, slag loss, rejected heats, casting loss, and billet rejection in coordination with the relevant departments. Optimize raw material utilization and production efficiency without compromising chemical composition or product quality. Prepare heat-wise and shift-wise reports covering production output, yield, energy consumption, rejection, and operating performance. Implement corrective actions to improve metallic recovery, reduce avoidable losses, and control steelmaking cost per metric ton. Prepare production schedules according to order requirements, raw material availability, and delivery targets. Monitor rolling speed, production temperature, mill synchronization, and machine performance to maintain continuous production. Ensure optimum mill utilization and achievement of daily and monthly production targets. Billet Reheating Furnace Management Supervise billet charging, furnace operation, heating zones, soaking time, and billet discharge. Maintain proper billet heating temperatures according to billet size, steel grade, and rolling requirements. Monitor furnace efficiency, fuel consumption, scale formation, and oxidation losses. Rolling Pass Schedule, Roll & Guide Setting Ensure correct pass schedule, roll groove selection, roll gap, and guide alignment for different product sizes. Supervise roll and guide setting, roll changes, size changeovers, and trial production. Maintain proper coordination between roughing, intermediate, and finishing stands. Troubleshoot cobbles, misrolling, bar twisting, guide failure, roll damage, and dimensional variations. Reduce changeover time, startup losses, rolling defects, and production downtime. Product Quality Control Ensure finished MS Rod / Deformed Bar meets approved specifications and applicable BSTI / BDS or other required standards. job_description: Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Officer PRANTIC Unnayan Society (PRANTIC), a national NGO established in 1998, invites applications from qualified and experienced candidates for the position of Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) Officer under the Bangladesh-Rohingya Humanitarian Response and Localization Program, PRANTIC Pooled Fund, Phase-5. Project Duration:  1 July–31 December 2026 (Possibilities of Expansion) Duty Station:  PRANTIC Regional Office, Ukhiya, Cox’s Bazar Employment Type:  Full-time, project-based Reports to:  Project Manager, with additional reporting responsibility to the Executive Director on assigned organizational MEAL functions About the Position Project:  Bangladesh-Rohingya Humanitarian Response and Localization Program Duty Station:  Project Office, Ukhiya, Cox’s Bazar Reports to:  Project Manager/Regional Manager Additional Reporting Line:  Executive Director Employment Type:  Project-based PRANTIC has been working in the Rohingya humanitarian response in Cox’s Bazar since 2018. Under the BRAC-managed Pooled Fund initiative, PRANTIC is implementing education activities to improve access to quality and inclusive education for Rohingya children. The MEAL Officer will lead day-to-day monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning functions for the Pooled Fund Education Project and provide technical MEAL support to other ongoing PRANTIC projects, including EMPOWER, GRACE and SEEMA, in Rohingya camps and host communities. The successful candidate will strengthen data quality, field monitoring, accountability mechanisms, evidence-based reporting and organizational learning to improve programme quality and demonstrate results. Key Responsibilities Develop and maintain an integrated MEAL plan, monitoring schedule, indicator tracking system and project databases. Conduct regular field monitoring visits to Community-Based Learning Facilities (CBLFs) and other project locations in Rohingya camps and host communities. Collect, verify, analyse and report quantitative and qualitative programme data against approved indicators, targets and results frameworks. Conduct Data Quality Assessments (DQA), verify reported achievements against source documents, identify discrepancies and follow up on corrective actions. Develop and maintain monitoring tools, questionnaires, databases and digital data collection systems using KoboToolbox or similar platforms. Monitor learner enrolment, attendance, retention, learning outcomes, classroom quality, gender equality and disability inclusion. Support assessments, evaluations, outcome monitoring, quarterly progress reporting, MIS updates and 5W reporting, as applicable. Support PRANTIC’s Community Feedback and Response Mechanism (CFRM), ensuring accessible, confidential and timely handling and referral of feedback and complaints. Document lessons learned, good practices, case studies and innovations, and provide practical recommendations for programme improvement. Provide technical guidance and capacity building to project staff, field teams, Teaching Volunteers and other relevant personnel on monitoring, data quality, documentation and reporting. Maintain organized and secure MEAL records and provide verified data and supporting evidence for BRAC, donors, audits and external monitoring. Coordinate with project teams, PRANTIC’s central MEAL and programme teams, the Education Sector and relevant humanitarian stakeholders. Safeguarding and Organizational Commitment The successful candidate must comply with PRANTIC’s safeguarding, child protection, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), Code of Conduct, Community Feedback and Response Mechanism (CFRM), confidentiality and data protection policies. All monitoring and data collection activities must follow informed-consent, safeguarding and Do No Harm principles. Female candidates and candidates with relevant experience in the Rohingya humanitarian response are particularly encouraged to apply.
